title: Foundations, Package Skeleton, And Contract Loop
objective: Create the standalone Server V2 package, boot a minimal Hono server, and establish the generated contract loop that later phases will build on.

steps.name: Create the new server package
steps.description: Add `apps/server-v2/` as a real workspace package with its own `package.json`, source tree, and clear ownership boundary so new server work does not land in legacy server files.
successFactors: `apps/server-v2/` is part of the workspace and can be installed and typechecked independently.
The package structure matches the planned `app.ts`, `cli.ts`, `routes/`, `services/`, `schemas/`, `middleware/`, `context/`, `adapters/`, `bootstrap/`, and `database/` shape.
No new Server V2 runtime code is added under `apps/server/src/**`.

steps.name: Register root scripts and workspace wiring
steps.description: Add root and package-level scripts for starting Server V2, generating OpenAPI, generating the SDK, and running contract checks so later phases can rely on one standard command graph.
successFactors: There is a one-shot contract generation path and a clearly named dev path.
Workspace filtering or package naming is stable enough for later agents to reuse without renaming scripts again.
Script names line up with `prds/server-v2-plan/sdk-generation.md` and `prds/server-v2-plan/local-dev.md`.

steps.name: Boot a minimal Hono app
steps.description: Create `src/app.ts` and `src/cli.ts` so the new server can start as its own process, listen on a port, and serve requests without being mounted under the old server.
successFactors: Running the Server V2 dev command starts a standalone process.
The server is not mounted under a legacy `/v2` path inside the current server.
Startup logs identify Server V2 clearly enough for debugging.

steps.name: Define the request context model
steps.description: Add typed request context and dependency wiring so handlers do not reach directly into global state and later phases can inject DB, auth, runtime, and service dependencies consistently.
successFactors: Handlers receive typed context instead of ad hoc globals.
The context model can grow without forcing route rewrites in later phases.
There is a clear place to attach auth actor, request ID, and shared services.

steps.name: Add baseline middleware
steps.description: Implement first-pass middleware for request IDs, structured request logging, error translation, and response finalization so the server starts with consistent HTTP behavior.
successFactors: Every request can be traced with a stable request ID.
Errors are returned in one consistent envelope instead of ad hoc text or mixed JSON shapes.
Middleware ordering is explicit and documented in code.

steps.name: Lock route namespace conventions
steps.description: Define the base route organization for workspace-first resources and `/system/*` server-level surfaces so later agents do not invent competing naming patterns.
successFactors: Workspace-first resource patterns are explicit and reusable.
Server-level operational routes live under `/system/*`.
The chosen route layout matches `prds/server-v2-plan/plan.md` and `prds/server-v2-plan/ideal-flow.md`.

steps.name: Add initial system routes
steps.description: Implement minimal boot routes like root info, `/system/health`, and metadata routes so the package can prove that it starts and serves typed responses.
successFactors: A health route works end to end from the standalone process.
The route responses already use the shared schema and error conventions.
Tests or smoke checks prove the server boots independently.

steps.name: Create shared schema helpers
steps.description: Add shared schema utilities for params, query, error bodies, standard success wrappers, timestamps, and IDs so route definitions stay uniform as the API grows.
successFactors: Common schema pieces are reusable instead of copy-pasted per route.
Error and success payloads can be documented once and reused.
Later phases can add route schemas without redefining primitives.

steps.name: Annotate routes for OpenAPI generation
steps.description: Integrate Hono route definitions with typed schemas and the chosen OpenAPI tooling so the running app is also the contract source of truth.
successFactors: The OpenAPI spec is generated from Hono route definitions rather than handwritten.
Operation IDs and schema names are stable and readable.
There is no parallel manual contract file to keep in sync.

steps.name: Generate `openapi/openapi.json`
steps.description: Add a script that loads the Server V2 app and emits `apps/server-v2/openapi/openapi.json` exactly as described in the plan docs.
successFactors: The generated spec lands at `apps/server-v2/openapi/openapi.json`.
Regeneration is deterministic when the contract does not change.
The generation command succeeds locally without manual patching.

steps.name: Create the reusable SDK package scaffold
steps.description: Add `packages/openwork-server-sdk/` with package metadata, config, and source layout so the generated client has a stable home and later handwritten helpers can live beside it.
successFactors: The SDK package is a workspace package with stable exports.
The package layout matches the planned `generated/` plus `src/index.ts` and `src/streams/**` split.
The app can depend on the workspace package directly.

steps.name: Configure SDK generation with `@hey-api/openapi-ts`
steps.description: Add the generator config and package scripts that turn `apps/server-v2/openapi/openapi.json` into the reusable TypeScript client package.
successFactors: SDK generation succeeds from the generated OpenAPI file.
The generator version is pinned exactly as recommended in the plan.
The generated output is committed in a predictable layout.

steps.name: Expose stable SDK entrypoints
steps.description: Add handwritten exports in `packages/openwork-server-sdk/src/index.ts` so app code imports stable package entrypoints instead of raw generator internals.
successFactors: App code does not need to import from `generated/**` directly.
There is an obvious future home for SSE helpers and transport utilities.
Generated and handwritten code compile together cleanly.

steps.name: Add placeholder SSE helper structure
steps.description: Create the initial `src/streams/**` layout in the SDK package and define the pattern future streaming helpers will use, even if the first real SSE endpoint lands in a later phase.
successFactors: There is a reserved place for handwritten streaming helpers.
The package layout matches the assumptions in `sdk-generation.md`.
Later phases can add typed SSE helpers without reorganizing the package.

steps.name: Create watcher scripts for contract regeneration
steps.description: Add repo-local watch scripts for OpenAPI and SDK generation so local development does not depend on fragile third-party watch behavior.
successFactors: There is a watcher for `apps/server-v2/src/**` -> OpenAPI regeneration.
There is a watcher for `openapi/openapi.json` -> SDK regeneration.
The scripts are shaped so later phases can extend them instead of replacing them.

steps.name: Add one-shot contract drift checks
steps.description: Create a CI-safe command that regenerates the spec and SDK and fails if a git diff appears, matching the contract discipline described in the planning docs.
successFactors: There is one canonical command for local and CI contract checks.
Generated artifacts do not drift silently.
The command can be reused in future CI or pre-merge automation.

steps.name: Add foundation tests
steps.description: Write the first tests for standalone server boot, health response shape, OpenAPI generation, and SDK generation so the new package is not validated only by manual smoke checks.
successFactors: A failing boot or broken spec generation is caught by automated tests.
The tests cover both runtime start and contract artifact generation.
The tests are fast enough to run regularly during future phases.

steps.name: Capture unresolved foundation assumptions
steps.description: If package naming, route naming, generator output, or startup conventions still have unresolved ambiguity, record them in `open-questions.md` and proceed with the best guess rather than leaving silent assumptions in code.
successFactors: Important assumptions are written down instead of hidden in implementation choices.
Any foundation-level uncertainty is visible to later phases.
Phase 1 ends with a stable enough platform for Phase 2 and Phase 4 to begin.
